subject: Recap + next steps: deployment needs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps: deployment needs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary from today's discovery:
- Primary use: product search and personalized recommendations in your web & mobile apps (low-latency inference required).
- Current baseline: legacy GPU cluster + inference proxy from OtherAI; peak concurrent requests ~120, p95 latency target <250ms.
- Data sensitivity: user PII occasionally in prompts; legal is concerned about data residency and auditability.
- Cost target: reduce per-1k-token inference cost vs current self-hosted spend.

Deployment options we discussed (very high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest path, no infra ops, transparent per-token billing, great for quick experimentation and can be production for lower-regulated workloads.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools we manage for you, predictable throughput and cost, better for sustained traffic where you want committed latency SLOs.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — customer-managed networking and optional on-prem package for regulated data, integrates with your KMS/HSM and audit logs.

Open questions we called out (please confirm if any of these are wrong):
- True peak qps and average token lengths during peak?
- Are there contractual data residency/GDPR constraints requiring EU-only hosting?
- Is any inference executed entirely inside your network (air-gapped) for some cohorts?

Suggested next steps:
- Tech deep-dive (45 min) with Dev to map throughput, batch sizing, and integration approach — can you share a couple of time windows next week?
- I attached a short one-pager that compares Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Also attaching a draft SLA for your review.

Attachments: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf; SLA-draft-30days.pdf

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Notes: sending to Lauren to loop in CSM for renewal/transition planning if we move off the legacy cluster.

From: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: deployment needs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Marissa, thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Peak qps: roughly 100–130 during campaigns, average seq length ~120 tokens, but some batching on our side (we currently batch up to 8).
- Our legal/compliance folks are leaning toward wanting the option for Private/VPC for any workloads that touch payment/PII; they might accept Dedicated if we get firm audit logs + SOC2 evidence.
- We do have a subset of inference that currently runs on an isolated rack (air-gapped for legacy fraud models) — migrating that will be sensitive.

We'd like to see the migration options for: (A) quick move from OtherAI hosted API to Redwood Hosted with minimal changes, (B) lift to Dedicated for predictable latency and (C) full Private/VPC plan — especially the migration effort and estimated timeline/cost for each.

Are you able to share a rough migration playbook before the call? Also cc'ing our legal contact in case they want to join the next thread: Acme Retail Legal <legal@acme-retail.com>.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Greene, Director of Product Engineering | Acme Retail
tom.greene@acme-retail.com | (646) 555-9876

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 17:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: deployment needs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Tom — great context, that's exactly the level of detail we need. I've attached a short migration playbook and the one-pager that lays out tradeoffs. High-level answers inline:

A) Quick move to Redwood Hosted:
- Effort: low (API-compatible endpoints, same SDK patterns). You can keep client-side batching and address mapping largely the same.
- Timeline: prototyping in days, pilot in 1–2 weeks for low-risk subsets.
- When to choose: when you prioritize speed-to-market and lower upfront cost.

B) Lift to Dedicated capacity:
- Effort: moderate (capacity planning, initial reserved commit, network whitelisting). We help with migration plans and warm-up.
- Timeline: 2–6 weeks depending on procurement and capacity commit.
- When to choose: predictable traffic, tighter latency SLOs, and want SLO-backed guarantees.

C) Private (VPC/on-prem):
- Effort: high (networking, KMS/HSM integration, air-gapped validation if required).
- Timeline: 6–12 weeks typical for VPC; on-prem longer depending on rack/ops.
- When to choose: regulated workloads, strict data residency, or air-gapped requirements.

I'll let Dev follow up with a short checklist of technical details we'll need to scope each path (throughput targets, sequence length distribution, current GPU types, inference pipeline, etc.).

Next step: can you propose 2 slots next week for a 45-min technical call? Wed/Thu mornings PST work well for us.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: deployment-options-one-pager.pdf; SLA-draft-30days.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Greene <tom.greene@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: deployment needs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Tom — quick technical checklist to help us size a recommendation and prepare migration estimates. Reply inline if you can, or paste answers in a doc we can access.

Required items:
- Average and peak qps (you gave 100–130 peak; can you confirm rolling 5m peak and sustained 1h peak?)
- Typical sequence length distribution (p50/p95/p99) and percent of requests that include PII.
- Current batching strategy and whether the client-side batching is plumbed into a request queue (yes/no).
- Current inference stack: model format (e.g., HF/ggml/OtherAI proprietary), serving frontend (NGINX + proxy vs custom), and GPU types (V100/A100/RTX?).
- Failover expectations: if Dedicated capacity is behind, do you want automatic fallback to Hosted model variants?
- Compliance: list of required audits/certifications (SOC2, ISO27001, etc.) and any legal contacts for contracts.

Attachments: redwood-migration-playbook.docx

Helpful to know but not required:
- Expected growth rate (q/q) over next 6 months; burst patterns (campaign-driven); and SLOs by route (search vs recommendations).

I'll consolidate answers and produce a comparative TCO + timeline for the three modes. Happy to do the 45-min call Wed 03/04 10am PST if that works for you.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
